pillarForecast.why: Chargers (the one non-luring enemy) are gone and late rocks sit between v13's A and B; every pursuer now chases, so kills stay his doing. Expect the removal to be absorbed silently.

Within one session the 'daily' course is simply the same course every run. Freshness, his stated meta-loop value ('new worlds'), is what this slice lacks; expect 'samey' or a request for worlds/missions late in the session.
A fixed course makes improvement legible: he learns where rocks and mines are and the best score climbs. 'Learning' and 'new best' should appear.
No checkpoints means every run is a full flight from sector 1 (60-100s when it goes well); he wins from the start sometimes, so runs keep their build-up.
The ghost is a labelled hollow circle in a distinct blue; small chance (~10%) it reads as clutter among pursuers or confuses him when it vanishes where his best run ended.

Slightly easier without chargers (bots 3.9-4.0 vs 3.7-3.8) and he called v13 'a bit too easy maybe'; a 'too easy' tag on a winning run is plausible (~15%), though the score gives him a new way to be greedy and die.

biggestRisk: He experiences 'same course every run', not 'a new course every day': the date seed only shows tomorrow, and within today's session the slice is one fixed course plus a number and a passive circle. He already predicted this himself ('that will probably lower the longevity'), so after a new best or two expect the enthusiasm to flatten into 'fun, but what keeps me coming back?', a late meh, and a request for the next layer (missions, worlds, other players' ghosts or a collidable race) rather than any complaint about the flight.
abVerdict: Leans B, and he names the ghost (~60%), because it is visible, labelled and his own pick ('scores and ghosts', the race idea). He will narrate it as a moment ('I passed my ghost', 'it was like racing myself') and immediately extend it: other players' ghosts, a leaderboard, or a ghost he can bump or lure chasers onto. A runs rarely mention its absence (~15%). Small chance (~15-20%) he finds it neutral or distracting and says the score is what matters.
